triage_reasoning: C3 is a secreted plasma protein synthesized primarily by the liver and macrophages. It circulates in blood as a soluble alpha-beta disulfide-linked heterodimer (~185 kDa). It has no transmembrane domain, no GPI anchor, and no known stable membrane partner that would co-traffic it to the cell surface. Checking each contextual bucket: (1) cell_state_induced — C3 deposits covalently on opsonized targets via its thioester-mediated attachment, but this is matrix/surface deposition on pathogens/debris, not PM display of the C3 protein body accessible from outside a host cell. (2) tissue_restricted_surface — no evidence of lineage-specific PM display. (3) lysosomal_exocytosis — not documented. (4) dual_localization — no evidence of a stable PM pool; covalent deposition on cells is on target cells/pathogens, not on C3-secreting cells. (5) stable_surface_attachment — opsonization deposits C3b/iC3b on target surfaces, but this reflects extracellular covalent attachment to glycoproteins/carbohydrates on those target cells, not the C3-producing cell's own PM. No antibody/ADC/CAR-T programs target C3 on a host cell surface. Anti-C3 therapeutics (e.g., pegcetacoplan) neutralize the soluble circulating form. Verdict: secreted_only.

executive_summary.one_paragraph: C3 is state-dependently surface-accessible as a secreted complement protein that deposits covalently onto target cell and pathogen surfaces after proteolytic activation — not a transmembrane protein on its producing cell. Supportive but indirect evidence: live-cell flow cytometry documents C3b/iC3b deposition on bacterial surfaces with serum controls (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_06), on vaginal epithelial cells during Candida infection (a1_evi_09), and on virus-infected host cells (a1_evi_11); immunofluorescence confirms C3 on human photoreceptors (a1_evi_15) and glomerular surfaces in disease (a1_evi_17). Surface presence is strictly state-gated, requiring complement activation; deposition increases in disease states including C3 glomerulopathy, renal ischemic injury, and thromboinflammatory conditions (a2_evi_21, a2_evi_15, a2_evi_24), and is suppressed by viral persistence (a2_evi_27). A massive circulating soluble C3 pool in plasma is the dominant antibody-decoy risk (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_22); moderate conformational epitope masking applies to the thioester domain in native C3 (a1_evi_02).
executive_summary.accessibility_context_summary: Surface-accessible only after complement activation, when C3b/iC3b deposits covalently onto target cell and pathogen surfaces; not stably displayed on the plasma membrane of C3-producing cells, and strictly absent from surfaces in the absence of complement triggering.

filters.expression_level_rationale: C3 is produced at high levels by hepatocytes as the dominant source of circulating complement (a2_evi_01); serum/plasma C3 concentrations are among the highest of any complement protein (a2_evi_29, a2_evi_22). Extrahepatic expression in immune cells, epithelial cells, and fibroblasts is moderate (a2_evi_03, a2_evi_07).
filters.expression_breadth_rationale: C3 expression is documented across liver, blood/immune cells, spleen, kidney, skin, retina, esophagus, placenta, brain, and adipose tissue (a2_evi_01, a2_evi_03, a2_evi_07, a2_evi_09, a2_evi_10, a2_evi_12, a2_evi_15, a2_evi_20, a2_evi_28), qualifying as pan-tissue.
filters.surface_specificity_rationale: C3 is primarily a secreted/soluble protein with a large intracellular complosome pool in T cells, hepatocytes, and FRCs (a2_evi_04, a2_evi_08, a2_evi_06); surface-deposited C3b/iC3b is state-dependent and occurs only on complement-activated target surfaces (a1_evi_06, a2_evi_22), making the overall profile mixed rather than surface-dominant.
filters.has_known_ligand_rationale: C3b binds complement receptors CR1 (CD35), CR3 (CD11b/CD18), and CR4 (CD11c/CD18) as validated endogenous ligand-receptor pairs; C3a binds C3aR as its cognate receptor — well-characterized natural biology (a2_evi_22, a2_evi_23).
filters.low_endogenous_expression_rationale: C3 is produced at high levels by hepatocytes as the dominant source of circulating complement (a2_evi_01); serum/plasma C3 concentrations are among the highest of any complement protein (a2_evi_29, a2_evi_22). Extrahepatic expression in immune cells, epithelial cells, and fibroblasts is moderate (a2_evi_03, a2_evi_07).
filters.overexpression_surface_localization_obse: No method observation pairs an overexpression/mixed expression system with a direct or supportive surface-accessibility readout.

surface_evidence.grade_rationale: The critical interpretive issue for C3 is WHAT is being detected at the surface and ON WHICH CELL. C3 is a secreted protein; its surface accessibility arises from covalent deposition of C3b/iC3b fragments onto TARGET cell surfaces (pathogens, host cells under complement attack), NOT from stable PM display on the C3-producing cell. With that framing, multiple direct methods confirm C3b/iC3b surface accessibility on target cells: (1) live-cell flow cytometry on A. baumannii bacteria using NHS vs heat-inactivated serum controls, showing significant C3b/iC3b deposition (a1_evi_05, a1_evi_06); (2) flow cytometry on human vaginal epithelial cells detecting C3b-positive fractions increasing with Candida infection (a1_evi_07, a1_evi_09); (3) flow synaptometry on isolated synaptosomes measuring C3b surface deposition (a1_evi_10); (4) IF on human photoreceptors (a1_evi_15) and rat glomerular tissue (a1_evi_17). These span live-cell flow and immunofluorescence — two distinct direct method classes — anchoring direct_multi_method. One live-cell flow study found C3b absent on opsonized platelets (a1_evi_24), a context-specific negative that does not contradict deposition on other target surfaces. Expression-only observations (a1_evi_22, a1_evi_23, a1_evi_26, a1_evi_27) confirm intracellular C3 in producing cells but do not establish PM display. Graded direct_multi_method for C3b/iC3b surface deposition on target cells, with state_dependence high (complement activation required).

contradicting_evidence.claim: C3 is canonically a secreted serum protein that circulates in soluble form and only becomes surface-associated after proteolytic cleavage to C3b, which then deposits covalently onto pathogen surfaces. There is no stable plasma-membrane display on the producing cell. This review-level assertion directly refutes the hypothesis that C3 is a surface-accessible antigen on human cells.
contradicting_evidence.likely_explanation: C3 is a classical secreted complement protein; its transient covalent deposition onto opsonized targets (pathogens, apoptotic cells) is mechanistically distinct from stable transmembrane or GPI-anchored surface display on the producing cell.

contradicting_evidence.claim: In iPSC-derived retinal pigment epithelium cells, C3 and its processing fragments are either secreted/shed into the apical compartment or retained intracellularly, with no evidence of stable plasma-membrane display. HM cells secrete C3a, C3(H2O), and iC3b, while LM cells retain C3 fragments intracellularly; immunofluorescence shows apical (not basolateral/PM) localization and intracellular presence of the intact C3 β chain.
contradicting_evidence.likely_explanation: RPE cells are polarized epithelial cells that synthesize and secrete C3 apically; intracellular retention in less mature cells likely reflects biosynthetic intermediates in the secretory pathway rather than surface-targeted protein. Neither pattern supports stable PM display.

contradicting_evidence.claim: Flow cytometry on live, non-permeabilized human platelets failed to detect C3b deposition on platelet surfaces even under conditions (E. coli-induced aggregation) where C3-dependent functional effects were observed. This directly contradicts the assumption that C3b fragment deposition on the platelet plasma membrane mediates the functional outcome.
contradicting_evidence.likely_explanation: C3 may act via a fluid-phase or indirect mechanism (e.g., anaphylatoxin signaling through C3aR) rather than covalent surface deposition on platelets; alternatively, C3b deposition may be below the detection threshold of the flow cytometry assay used.

subcellular_localization.rationale: C3 is canonically a secreted plasma protein produced primarily by hepatocytes (a2_evi_01, a2_evi_22, a2_evi_29). Review and functional evidence confirm it circulates as a soluble serum protein and only becomes surface-associated after proteolytic activation and covalent deposition via its thioester bond onto target surfaces (a2_evi_22, a2_evi_23). C3(H2O) is constitutively present in plasma (a2_evi_29).

dual_localization.condition: in hepatocytes, T cells, and FRCs (intracellular complosome pool)
dual_localization.rationale: Review evidence describes intracellular C3 in hepatocytes playing roles in autophagy, ER function, and lipid homeostasis (a2_evi_04). Intracellular C3 activation in T cells regulates homeostasis and effector differentiation (a2_evi_08). FRCs upregulate intracellular C3 upon SFTSV infection (a2_evi_06).

dual_localization.condition: on activated host cells or pathogen surfaces after complement activation
dual_localization.rationale: C3b becomes covalently deposited on target surfaces via thioester transacylation upon complement activation (a2_evi_23). C3(H2O) associates with activated platelets and endothelial cells in thromboinflammatory states (a2_evi_24). Surface C3 deposition on virus-infected respiratory cells detected by live-cell flow cytometry (a2_evi_27).

dual_localization.condition: in C3 glomerulopathy and renal ischemic injury
dual_localization.rationale: IHC in human kidney biopsies shows abnormal glomerular C3 deposition in C3 glomerulopathy due to alternative pathway dysregulation (a2_evi_21). C3 staining also detected in injured tubules in RIAKI by permeabilized IHC (a2_evi_15).

dual_localization.condition: in mature iPSC-derived RPE under high-maturation conditions
dual_localization.rationale: Permeabilized IF on HM iPSC-RPE shows apical localization of C3 protein with intracellular intact C3 β chain (a2_evi_10). Western blot confirms apical secretion of C3a, C3(H2O), iC3b from HM cells (a2_evi_11).
Permeabilized IF on fixed mouse cerebellar tissue shows C3-tagged VGLUT1+ presynaptic puncta, declining with age while overall C3 expression increases (a2_evi_28).

membrane_subdomains.rationale: Permeabilized IF on HM iPSC-derived RPE cells shows apical localization of C3 protein in mature retinal pigment epithelium (a2_evi_10).

anatomical_accessibility.rationale: Permeabilized IF directly observed C3 localizing to the apical surface of mature HM iPSC-RPE cells (a2_evi_10), with apical secretion of C3 fragments confirmed by western blot (a2_evi_11). Apical orientation in RPE faces the subretinal space, restricting access from the choroidal/blood side.

accessibility_modulation.change: Surface deposition of C3 is greatly reduced on persistently PIV5-infected respiratory cells compared to acutely infected cells, indicating viral persistence suppresses complement opsonization of host cell surfaces.
accessibility_modulation.accessibility_implication: Reduced C3 surface deposition on persistently infected cells means fewer C3b/iC3b epitopes accessible to extracellular binders; complement-targeting strategies would be less effective against persistently infected cells.

accessibility_modulation.change: Native C3 demonstrates highest binding to activated platelets expressing phospholipid-scrambled membranes compared to resting state; C3(H2O) also exists in bound form on activated platelets in thromboinflammatory disorders.
accessibility_modulation.accessibility_implication: Platelet activation exposes surface sites that recruit C3 and enable convertase formation; C3-derived epitopes become accessible on activated but not resting platelet surfaces.

accessibility_modulation.change: Abnormal glomerular C3 deposition (C3b/iC3b/C3c fragments) accumulates on glomerular surfaces in C3 glomerulopathy due to dysregulation of the complement alternative pathway.
accessibility_modulation.accessibility_implication: Glomerular surfaces in C3G are heavily opsonized with C3 fragments, making C3b/iC3b epitopes highly accessible to extracellular binders in this disease state.

accessibility_modulation.modulating_state: renal ischemia-associated acute kidney injury (RIAKI) tubules
accessibility_modulation.change: C3 protein staining is detected in injured kidney tubules in RIAKI patients, often surrounded by C5aR1-expressing myeloid cells, indicating C3 deposition on injured tubular surfaces.
accessibility_modulation.accessibility_implication: Injured tubular surfaces in RIAKI accumulate C3 deposits, providing accessible C3-derived epitopes for extracellular binders in the disease context.

accessibility_modulation.change: In high-maturation iPSC-RPE, C3 localizes apically and intact C3 β chain is present intracellularly; HM cells secrete increased C3a, C3(H2O), and iC3b apically. LM cells retain C3 fragments intracellularly without apical surface localization.
accessibility_modulation.accessibility_implication: Mature RPE cells display C3 apically, making it accessible to extracellular binders from the apical (subretinal) side; immature RPE retains C3 intracellularly, limiting extracellular accessibility.

accessibility_modulation.change: C3 is present both intracellularly (complosome) in T cells, hepatocytes, and FRCs — where it regulates autophagy, ER function, and immune effector responses — and extracellularly as a secreted/deposited complement protein on surfaces.
accessibility_modulation.accessibility_implication: The intracellular pool of C3 is not accessible to extracellular binders; only the secreted/deposited surface-associated fraction is targetable. The balance between pools varies by cell type and activation state.

accessibility_modulation.change: SFTSV infection significantly induces intracellular complement C3 production in splenic FRCs via the alternative pathway, generating active C3a — a cell-type-specific, infection-induced upregulation of C3 in non-immune stromal cells.
accessibility_modulation.accessibility_implication: Infection-induced intracellular C3 production in FRCs generates C3a locally; the intracellular nature limits direct extracellular binder access, but secreted C3a may be accessible in the extracellular milieu.

accessibility_modulation.modulating_state: pre-eclampsia or recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) placenta
accessibility_modulation.change: C3 protein levels are elevated in placentae from pre-eclampsia and RPL compared to normal placentae, suggesting overactivation of complement and increased C3 deposition in these obstetric disease states.
accessibility_modulation.accessibility_implication: Elevated C3 in diseased placentae may increase surface-deposited C3 fragments accessible to extracellular binders in PE and RPL, though direct surface localization data are not provided.

accessibility_modulation.change: Circulating C3a is elevated during aging in both humans and mice; age-associated macrophages expanding in visceral fat are the predominant source. C3-tagged presynaptic puncta decline in cerebellum despite overall complement factor increase with age.
accessibility_modulation.accessibility_implication: Aging increases systemic C3a availability and alters C3 deposition patterns at synapses; elevated circulating C3a is accessible to extracellular binders in aged individuals.

biological_context.grade_rationale: All four A2 axes are well-populated from independent sources: expression mapped across liver, spleen, kidney, skin, retina, esophagus, placenta, adipose, and plasma; subcellular localization pinned (intracellular complosome vs. secreted/deposited); anatomical accessibility documented (glomerular deposits, tubular staining, synaptic tagging); modulation evidence across disease states (CHB, T1D/T2D, aging, viral infection, EoE). Multiple primary assay types (IHC, IF, flow, scRNA-seq, RT-qPCR, WB) from ≥10 independent sources. Picture is coherent: C3 is a secreted/deposited complement protein with context-dependent intracellular roles. Grade: rich.

co_receptor_requirements.rationale: C3 is a secreted plasma protein that circulates as a soluble form and deposits onto surfaces via thioester-mediated covalent attachment after proteolytic activation (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_22). It has no transmembrane domain and no obligate escort or chaperone partner required for surface deposition. Membrane association is entirely driven by the reactive thioester bond in C3b (a1_evi_03, a1_evi_04).

shed_form.rationale: C3 is not a transmembrane protein and has no ectodomain to shed in the classical sense. The ledger documents proteolytic cleavage of soluble C3 to C3b/C3a by convertases (a1_evi_01, a1_evi_04), but this is activation of a circulating protein, not shedding of a membrane-anchored ectodomain. No sheddase releasing a membrane-tethered C3 ectodomain is documented.

secreted_form.rationale: C3 is constitutively present as a soluble protein in serum/plasma at high concentrations (a1_evi_01, a2_evi_22, a2_evi_29). It is the canonical secreted complement protein produced by hepatocytes (a2_evi_01). Circulating C3 and its fragments (C3a, C3(H2O), iC3b) are documented in plasma and serum (a2_evi_29, a2_evi_19), representing a massive soluble decoy pool for any circulating antibody targeting C3.

restricted_subdomain.rationale: In mature iPSC-RPE cells, C3 localizes apically (a1_evi_23, a2_evi_10), suggesting apical-surface restriction in polarized epithelial cells. However, C3 is primarily a secreted/deposited protein and deposits broadly on pathogen and host cell surfaces across many cell types (a1_evi_06, a1_evi_11, a2_evi_21). The apical restriction is cell-type-specific and does not represent a general accessibility barrier.

ecd_size_assessment.rationale: ECD length 1641 residues (>=200) -> large; computed deterministically from DeepTMHMM topology.

epitope_masking.rationale: C3 undergoes major conformational change upon activation: the thioester domain (TED) is buried in native C3 and exposed only after cleavage to C3b (a1_evi_02, a1_evi_03). Antibodies targeting neoepitopes in C3(D)/C3b conformations (e.g. clones 4SD17.3, 7D84.1) are distinct from those recognizing native C3 (a1_evi_14), confirming that key epitopes are conformationally masked in the native soluble form. No homo-oligomerization is predicted (deterministic: is_homo_oligomer=false) and no ledger evidence supports oligomeric masking.

evidence.claim: C3 is present in a soluble form in serum but becomes covalently deposited onto the surfaces of pathogens after proteolytic cleavage to C3b — establishing the canonical secreted-then-deposited topology with no stable PM display on the producing cell.

spans.quote: This system centres around complement C3, which is present in a soluble form in serum but becomes covalently deposited onto the surfaces of pathogens after proteolytic cleavage to C3b.

evidence.claim: Activated C3b binds to the surface of transformed cells through the thioester moiety (Cys-1010–Gln-1013) in the thioester-containing domain (TED); factors I and H then convert surface-bound C3b to iC3b. This defines the covalent surface-attachment mechanism of C3b and the topology of the deposited fragment.

spans.quote: Activated C3b species can bind to the surface of transformed cells through the activation of the thioester moiety Cys-1010-Gln-1013 in the thioester-containing domain (TED). 5 For the deactivation of C3b, factors I (FI) and H (FH) can convert the bound C3b into iC3b, which is followed by the release of a small C3f piece.

evidence.claim: C3 belongs to the AMCOM thioester protein family and contains a conserved furin cleavage site and the thioester linkage consensus sequence GCGEQ capable of forming a covalent bond with substrates via thioester transacylation — confirming the structural basis for surface deposition without a transmembrane anchor.

spans.quote: Each family member has several conserved sequence motifs, including a furin cleavage site and, with the exception of C5, the thioester linkage consensus sequence GCGEQ that is capable of forming a covalent bond with substrates through thioester transacylation.

evidence.claim: C3b becomes covalently attached to surface-exposed nucleophiles on target surfaces via transacylation mediated by its reactive internal thioester bond — direct mechanistic description of how C3b achieves surface localization on opsonized targets.

spans.quote: Complement activation on target surfaces drives the proteolytic activation of complement factor 3 (C3) to C3b, which becomes covalently attached to surface-exposed nucleophiles via a transacylation mediated by its reactive internal thioester bond.

evidence.claim: Flow cytometry protocol for measuring C3b/iC3b deposition on live bacterial surfaces: 10^6 CFU incubated with 25% normal human serum (NHS) or heat-inactivated serum (HIS) for 30 min at 37°C, then stained with mouse monoclonal antibody clone 6C9 (Millipore) against C3b/iC3b, detected with goat anti-mouse IgG-APC. Heat-inactivated serum served as negative control.

spans.quote: C3b/iC3b and C5b-8/C5b-9 (MAC) deposition on A. baumannii bacterial surface was assessed using flow cytometry as previously described ( 6 , 7 , 12 , 36 – 38 ). 10 6 CFU of A. baumannii was incubated with either 25% (the optimized concentration for differentiating between strains) normal human sera (NHS) or heat-inactivated human sera (HIS) for 30 minutes at 37°C, washed twice with PBS, followed by incubation in either the mouse monoclonal antibody 6C9 (Millipore) or aE11 (Abcam), in triplicate and detected using goat anti-mouse IgG-allophycocyanin (APC) (Invitrogen).

evidence.claim: Flow cytometry on live A. baumannii strains showed significant C3b/iC3b deposition on all three strains (encapsulated WT and two unencapsulated isogenic mutants), with significantly higher deposition on unencapsulated strains — direct surface-accessibility readout of C3b on bacterial surfaces using NHS vs HIS controls.

spans.quote: The levels of deposition of C3b/iC3b and C5b-8/C5b-9 differed significantly between the encapsulated AB5075 and unencapsulated strains ( Figures 1A, B ).

evidence.claim: Monoclonal antibody clone 1H8 (Hycult Biotech, Uden, Netherlands) used for detection of human C3b/iC3b/C3d in flow cytometry assays on vaginal epithelial cells — antibody reagent identifier for surface C3 detection method.

spans.quote: The monoclonal antibodies mouse anti-human complement component-5 (C5) (clone 10B6), mouse anti-human C5a/C5a des-arg (clone 2042) and mouse anti-human C3b/iC3b/C3d (clone 1H8) were kindly provided by Hycult Biotech (Uden, The Netherlands).

evidence.claim: Flow cytometry on vaginal epithelial cells (VECs) showed approximately 49.8% of uninfected VECs were positive for C3, increasing non-significantly to 63.2–63.8% after Candida infection — direct surface/intracellular C3 detection in epithelial cells (permeabilization status unspecified; likely includes intracellular pool).

spans.quote: Our results show that approximately half of the VECs analyzed were positive for C3 (49.8%), with a non-significant increase after infection with either the Colonizing (63.2%) or VVC (63.8%) strain ( Figure 1 a).

confidence_reasoning: Confidence is moderate for two reasons. First, the surface-accessibility evidence is indirect for the key question of whether C3-derived fragments on host cell surfaces are targetable: most direct readouts (live-cell flow, immunofluorescence) measure deposition on pathogens or in disease-state tissues, and the permeabilization status of several epithelial-cell assays is unspecified, leaving uncertainty about whether intracellular or surface pools are being detected. Second, the massive circulating soluble C3 pool in plasma (documented across multiple independent sources) represents a high-severity antibody-decoy risk that substantially limits the practical accessibility of any surface-deposited form. Lifting confidence would require live-cell, non-permeabilized flow cytometry on defined human cell types under complement-activating conditions, with orthogonal surface biotinylation or proximity-labeling confirmation of the deposited C3b epitope accessibility. The triage verdict of 'secreted_only' is partially overridden here because direct evidence of C3b surface deposition on host cells exists, but the decoy concern and indirect evidence base justify moderate rather than high confidence.
